Title: EcoTaskSched: a hybrid machine learning approach for energy- efficient task scheduling in IoT- based fog-cloud environments

 The widespread adoption of cloud services has posed several challenges, primarily revolving around 
energy and resource efficiency. Integrating cloud and fog resources can help address these challenges 
by improving fog-cloud computing environments. Nevertheless, the search for optimal task allocation 
and energy management in such environments continues. Existing studies have introduced notable 
solutions; however, it is still a challenging issue to efficiently utilize these heterogeneous cloud 
resources and achieve energy-efficient task scheduling in fog-cloud of things environment.  To tackle 
these challenges, we propose a novel ML-based EcoTaskSched model, which leverages deep learning 
for energy-efficient task scheduling in fog-cloud networks. The proposed hybrid model integrates 
Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) with Bidirectional Log-Short Term Memory (BiLSTM) to 
enhance energy-efficient schedulability and reduce energy usage while ensuring QoS provisioning. 
The CNN model efficiently extracts workload features from tasks and resources, while the BiLSTM 
captures complex sequential information, predicting optimal task placement sequences.  A real fog-
cloud environment is implemented using the COSCO framework for the simulation setup together 
with four physical nodes from the Azure B2s plan to test the proposed model. The DeFog benchmark 
is used to develop task workloads, and data collection was conducted for both normal and intense 
workload scenarios. Before preprocessing the data was normalized, treated with feature engineering 
and augmentation, and then split into training and test sets.  To evaluate performance, the proposed 
EcoTaskSched model demonstrated superiority by significantly reducing energy consumption and 
improving job completion rates compared to baseline models. Additionally, the EcoTaskSched model 
maintained a high job completion rate of 85%, outperforming GGCN and BiGGCN. It also achieved a 
lower average response time, and SLA violation rates, as well as increased throughput, and reduced 
execution cost compared to other baseline models.  In its optimal configuration, the EcoTaskSched 
model is successfully applied to fog-cloud computing environments, increasing task handling efficiency 
and reducing energy consumption while maintaining the required QoS parameters. Our future studies 
will focus on long-term testing of the EcoTaskSched model in real-world IoT environments. We will 
also assess its applicability by integrating other ML models, which could provide enhanced insights for 
optimizing scheduling algorithms across diverse fog-cloud settings.

In recent years, cloud computing has revolutionized how business organizations manage and deploy their ICT1 
resources by offering scalable, on-demand services2 to service users. This paradigm shift enables businesses 
to reduce infrastructure costs related to hardware procurement, maintenance, and energy consumption 
by transferring these responsibilities to cloud service providers3. However, the exponential growth in cloud 
service usage including application delivery, storage, computation, and resource allocation has led to significant 
challenges, particularly in energy efficiency and resource management. Fog computing4, an extension of cloud 
computing5, aims to address some of these challenges6 by decentralizing data processing closer to the data 
source7,8. This approach reduces latency and bandwidth usage, which are critical for real-time applications 
such as the Internet of Things (IoT)9, autonomous vehicles10, smart grids11, smart farming12, smart cities13, 
industries14,15 and healthcare16,17. By processing data at the edge of the network, fog computing minimizes the 
need for data to travel long distances to centralized cloud servers, thereby enhancing performance and reliability. 
Fog-cloud computing environments inherit the strengths of both cloud and fog computing. The hybrid model 
leverages the centralized processing power of the cloud while utilizing the proximity and low latency of fog 
nodes18. Additionally, it supports a wide range of applications, from consumer-oriented services to critical 
industrial operations. Such an environment can efficiently handle the vast amounts of data generated by IoT 
devices, enabling real-time analytics and decision-making more convenient19. Another key benefit of fog-cloud 
computing is its ability to provide a scalable and flexible infrastructure. Organizations can dynamically allocate 
resources in a cost-effective manner20 to achieve optimal system performance.
Despite these prominent features, fog-cloud computing faces several design challenges, particularly in the 
context of task scheduling and energy efficiency21,22. Energy-efficient task scheduling is crucial to ensuring 
that computational tasks are assigned to the most appropriate resources, whether in the cloud or at the fog 
nodes. This requires sophisticated algorithms capable of balancing the load, minimizing energy consumption, 
and maintaining high levels of performance23. Recent advancements in artificial intelligence (AI) and machine 
learning (ML) have shown promise in addressing these challenges24. ML-based task scheduling algorithms 
optimize resource allocation by predicting workloads and dynamically adjusting task assignments and execution. 
Similarly, the growing demand for cloud services has led to increased power consumption in data centers. 
Intelligent systems can significantly reduce energy consumption and enhance the overall performance of the 
fog-cloud environment. In addition, data centers that host heterogeneous servers, storage, and network devices 
incur higher operating costs due to their capacity requirements. As these computing environments scale up and

In contrast, many researchers have adopted various ML techniques, carefully considering sampling data and 
feature sets to train and test scheduling policies in the context of fog-cloud computing environments. However, 
their published works contain shortcomings related to resource allocation, optimization, task scheduling, and 
power management in fog-cloud computing.
These challenges motivate us to clearly address this research challenge and provide a viable solution to the 
existing work in this domain. Therefore, this research study mainly focuses on developing an energy-efficient 
task scheduling framework, ensuring that each task is strictly assigned to either a fog or cloud node. This study 
aims to ensure that the response time does not exceed a maximum threshold, a minimum job completion 
rate is maintained under intense workloads, and SLA violations are limited to a fixed threshold in fog-cloud 
environments.
Inspired by the baseline models25,26, this research study extends our previously published work27 by proposing 
a novel ML-based hybrid scheduling approach called EcoTaskSched model. The goal of EcoTaskSched model 
is to improve workflow efficiency by scheduling energy-efficient tasks in fog and cloud resources. Additionally, 
it aims to reduce the energy footprint by leveraging advanced deep learning (DL) techniques. This is achieved 
through the concatenation of a CNN model with a BiLSTM network. When compared to existing research, 
the proposed EcoTaskSched model provides a viable solution. It ensures that all performance metrics required 
for various dynamic IoT applications are met for the first time in a fog-cloud environment. Our significant 
contributions in this research study include the following:
	1.	 The EcoTaskSched model is introduced as a novel task scheduling architecture integrating: (i) A CNN, which 
typically has multiple deep layers designed to detect and extract spatial patterns (feature sets) from tasks 
and system resources. (ii) A BiLSTM, combined with convolutional layers, to capture both future and past 
context from the input sequence to solve the research problem.
	2.	 The research problem is mathematically formulated through an objective function, subject to additional 
operating constraints. An algorithm is implemented to apply the proposed methodology for energy-efficient 
task scheduling in fog and cloud resources.
	3.	 Finally, we evaluate the performance of the proposed EcoTaskSched model through extensive experiments 
simulated using the Coupled Simulation and Container Orchestration (COSCO) framework under different 
workload scenarios. Simulation results show that the objective function is satisfied, indicating that energy 
consumption is minimized and QoS requirements are met for heterogeneous IoT applications in a fog-cloud 
computing environment.

an overview of ML-based models and the system architecture. Section "Proposed EcoTaskSched methodology"

Related work
This section reviews key contemporary approaches adopted by researchers. The focus is on integrating traditional 
scheduling and ML-based scheduling techniques to achieve energy efficiency for distributed resources in a fog-
cloud computing environment. The following subsections review related research relevant to our proposed 
research methodology.
Traditional algorithms in task scheduling
Traditional task scheduling algorithms have been foundational in managing computing resources in cloud 
computing environments. These algorithms aim to balance and optimize resource allocation while reducing 
uptime and energy consumption in major cloud computing projects. Some commonly used traditional scheduling 
algorithms include First-Come, First-Served (FCFS), Round Robin (RR), Max-Min, Min-Min, Priority-Aware, 
and Most Efficient Server First (MESF).
An Energy-Aware Task Scheduler (ETSG)28 uses a Genetic Algorithm (GA) to minimize both makespan 
and energy usage in cloud data centers. The proposed framework outperforms the Max-Min algorithm in 
reducing energy consumption and task execution time on VMs in cloud data centers. This is because the Max-
Min algorithm assigns the task with the highest processing time to the server. This method prioritizes long 
tasks, helping to balance the load on servers. However, the Max-Min system can lead to energy inefficiency, as 
it does not minimize the system’s total energy consumption. Similarly, a GA-based task scheduling approach29 
is proposed to uniformly distribute the load on VMs and minimize response time, which is a QoS requirement 
in a dynamic cloud environment. The proposed technique outperforms traditional scheduling methods such as 
FCFS and Greedy-based algorithms. Among these, FCFS is one of the simplest scheduling frameworks available. 
However, in FCFS, tasks are assigned inadvertently, without considering the specific needs or nature of tasks and 
resources in cloud paradigms. Although easy to implement, FCFS typically results in lower resource efficiency 
and higher energy consumption, as it does not account for server workloads or their ability to handle incoming 
tasks.

Many researchers have introduced modified versions of the basic Min-Min heuristic30 to address task 
scheduling issues. To achieve efficient system performance, the Optimized Min-Min (OMin-Min) mechanism31 
is proposed. It classifies scientific workflows and scheduling strategies based on existing scheduling algorithms 
(i.e. Min-Min, Max-Min, Modified Max-Min, and Round Robin) for different cloudlet sizes to achieve better 
execution time and optimal resource utilization in a cloud computing environment. However, these mechanisms 
are not well-suited for heterogeneous resources in a multi-cloud task scheduling environment32, as they do 
not consider differences among cloudlets (tasks) and assume that all resources are homogeneous. In contrast, 
MESF33 is a resource-aware scheduling framework that prioritizes tasks based on server efficiency. It identifies 
the most energy-efficient server for each task (job) and assigns tasks accordingly. Jobs are then allocated to the 
next most efficient server and continuing the process until all jobs are processed. This method can significantly 
reduce energy consumption while ensuring that response time constraints are met, compared to other random 
or less sophisticated scheduling methods. It is especially effective in heterogeneous environments where servers 
have varying capacities and energy profiles. An efficient task scheduling model using hybrid optimization 
techniques, incorporating Particle Swarm Grey Wolf Optimization (PSGWO), is proposed34 to identify optimal 
VMs and allocate resources to tasks in cloud computing environments. For tasks scheduling, a support vector 
machine (SVM) classifier is used to categorize VMs statuses into four different categories. Linear parameters 
(for average utilization) and nonlinear parameters (for underutilization) are identified to assess VM utilization. 
To ensure QoS, VM status, waiting time and task execution time are considered to evaluate system performance 
and overcome tasks scheduling issues. QoS-aware resource optimization strategies for constrained IoT systems 
coupled with cloud computing environments are proposed in27,35. In27, a hybrid queue scheduling (HQS) method 
is introduced, using non-preemptive priority queue scheduling (NP-PQS) for time-critical IoT traffic and FCFS 
for normal traffic to guarantee QoS requirements for resource-constrained devices in the communication 
network. The proposed optimization method reduces the utilization cost of cloud resources (RAM, CPU, and 
bandwidth) for different IoT applications on cloud servers. However, the NP-PQS scheme in cloud computing 
faces several challenges, such as handling workloads, scalability issues, and resource starvation. A QoS-aware data 
aggregation (QoS-DA) strategy for different IoT applications (on-demand, periodic, and critical) with varying 
latency and traffic rates is proposed in35 using a hierarchical clustering topology. The main objective of this 
strategy is to efficiently utilize the limited resources (RAM, CPU, network capacity, and storage) of relay devices 
in an IoT-enabled cloud computing network. Results show that the proposed strategy successfully optimized 
constrained resources, ensured QoS levels, and reduced execution time for IoT applications on cloud servers. 
However, such strategies come with several challenges, such as reduced data accuracy, vulnerable to data loss, and 
loss of data granularity. The research work in36 proposes a job-oriented scheduling model for efficient resource 
scheduling in a cloud environment. Tasks are scheduled based on user preferences and available resources. Three 
traditional scheduling algorithms, namely Preemptive Priority (PP), RR, and Shortest Remaining Time First 
(SRTF) are used for resource scheduling. Among these, SRTF incurred the lowest time parameters and remained 
the most efficient scheduling algorithm. A Security Oriented Deadline-Aware (SODA) workflow allocation 
strategy is proposed in37, ensuring that each task meets security precedence demands and deadline constraints 
to minimize risk probability in an Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS) deterministic cloud computing environment. 
The scientific workflow order is calculated based on the security upward rank of each task and then allocated to 
and executed on trustable VMs that ensure the task’s deadline and trust level. Simulation results show that SODA 
outperforms other strategies while reducing the risk probability of scientific workflows in the cloud systems.

An ANN-based dynamic VM consolidation algorithm is proposed in38 to optimize resources, reduce 
energy usage, and increase VM migration in a cloud environment. The proposed algorithm adaptively selects 
the best scheduling method based on cloud provider parameters and priority goals. The results demonstrate 
that, through higher VM migration, the proposed technique achieves better performance, minimizes energy 
consumption, and reduces SLA violations. The proposed model39, called the Cloud Service Orchestrator (CSO), 
employs cat-based swarm optimization for efficient resource management in data-intensive businesses to obtain 
optimal scheduling decisions and ensure QoS (e.g., energy efficiency, makespan) in the fog-cloud environment. 
The experiments are conducted using the COSCO40 framework, considering thermal, energy, and cooling 
models to find the optimal solution for the multi-objective scheduling issue in both real-world and simulated 
cloud environments. The experimental results demonstrate that the proposed model outperforms state-of-the-
art baseline models in terms of makespan, energy efficiency, and lower execution overhead in the fog-cloud 
environment.
Although CNNs are primarily used for visualization, they also have applications in cloud-based project design. 
CNNs can capture spatial patterns in data, which can be translated into meaningful resource management plans 
across nodes in a fog-cloud environment. By converting resource models into a 2D array format, CNNs can 
more effectively identify and predict task allocation, reducing energy consumption and improving efficiency. 
The proposed HUNTER scheduler uses a GGCN coupled with an RNN model to predict QoS parameters 
and make informed policy decisions that enhance performance and energy efficiency25. Similarly, the new 
HunterPlus scheduler extends the traditional GGCN model by utilizing a CNN scheduler, which outperforms 
the GGCN-based strategy in both job completion rates and energy usage per task. Specifically, it optimize QoS 
metrics to make scheduling decisions more efficiently26. In contrast, RL model offers a different approach by 
treating the scheduling challenge as a sequential decision-making process. In RL, the agent learns to make 
decisions by interacting with the environment and receiving feedback in the form of rewards or punishments. 
This approach is particularly useful in dynamic and unpredictable environments, where the agent can adjust 
its strategy based on the consequences of its actions. An RL-based model called Weighted Double Deep 
Q-Network-based Reinforcement Learning (WDDQN-RL) has been proposed to schedule multiple workflows 
and optimize resources. This approach results in a shorter makespan and reduced costs by continuously learning 
from system performance41. One notable deep reinforcement learning (DRL) system, called DeepEE42, employs 
a Parameterized Action Space based Deep Q-Network (PADQN), which optimizes work scheduling and cooling 
control of data centers concurrently at multiple sites to achieve energy efficiency. The proposed scheduling 
technique improves IT performance, enhances energy savings in cooling systems, and ensures service quality in 
cloud computing. To address the safety evaluation issue in cloud data centers, a model-assisted DRL technique 
called LyaSafe43 is proposed for cooling control to ensure compliance with strict safety standards. The primary 
objective of this work is to minimize carbon emissions and regulate the Rack Cooling Index (RCI) within a 
specified threshold. An end-to-end Deep Q Scheduler (DQS) task scheduling algorithm based on the DRL 
model is proposed in44 to address high dimensional scheduling issues in cloud computing. The proposed model 
uses a CNN to extract task features and output information about the VMs executing the task in the cloud 
environment. This model enhances scheduling accuracy and minimizes task execution time. To address the 
Task as a Service (TaaS) scheduling problem, a DRL-based TaaS Cloud (DRLTC) scheduling is proposed45 for 
the cloud environment. Tasks are scheduled based on their resource requirements and deadlines (time stamps). 
The proposed scheduling algorithm successfully schedules TaaS and achieves superior performance. A Hybrid 
ML technique called Resource Allocation Task Scheduling (RATS-HM)46, with combines efficient resource 
allocation with a security feature, is proposed for cloud computing. The proposed technique uses Improved 
Cat Swarm Optimization for Task Scheduling (ICSO-TS) with a short scheduler, which reduces execution time 
and increases system throughput in cloud computing. Additionally, a Group Optimization-based Deep Neural 
Network (GO-DNN) is used to optimize resource allocation, including load and bandwidth. Data encryption is 
applied to secure data storage. Simulation results show that the proposed RATS-HM provides security, minimizes 
makespan, and reduces energy consumption through efficient task scheduling in the cloud environment. In47, 
an automatic-scaling approach called Thoth is proposed, using Docker container technology for Platform as 
a Service (PaaS). Thoth automatically monitors resource utilization and dynamically allocates appropriate 
resources to each application. The Thoth algorithm is implemented using three approaches, namely Q-Learning, 
which optimizes computing resources more efficiently than rule-based and Neural Network (NN) algorithms. 
The authors conducted a systematic and comprehensive literature review to examine recent advancement in 
several approaches, including machine learning inference (MLI)48, clod start latency49,50, function placement51, 
proactive content caching52, function offloading53, computation offloading54, and scheduling mechanisms55 in 
a serverless computing environment. To handle the increasing number of modules that need to be executed on 
the Mobile Fog Computing (MFC), a Hidden Markov Model Auto-scaling Offloading (HMAO) method54 is 
proposed to find the best place for module execution in order to minimize energy consumption, execution time; 
optimize the execution time, network resource usage, and delay of the modules on the mobile, Fog, or Cloud. 
The results obtained demonstrate that the proposed method is superior to the First-Fit (FF) and Q-learning

Research problem
Although traditional task scheduling algorithms 27–31,33–36 have laid the foundation for business processes in cloud 
computing environments, they have notable limitations. In particular, they lack the ability to dynamically adapt to

efficiency. For example, priority-aware and FCFS methods often fail to consider the characteristics of tasks and 
VMs, ultimately resulting in poor system performance. In contrast, ML-based scheduling models25,26,47,38,39, 41–46 
offer significant improvements over traditional scheduling methods for business processes by providing scalable, 
data-driven solutions capable of handling today’s complex fog-cloud computing environments. However, ML-
based scheduling models also have several deficiencies. ML-based algorithms are often trained on a manually 
selected set of features (labels) from sample data to design scheduling policies. Acquiring a large number of 
labeled samples is challenging in practice, and the quality of these features directly impacts the effectiveness of 
the scheduling algorithm. Additionally, most trained models are environment-specific, which can ultimately 
lead to system failure. For example, RL models are unable to adapt to hosts running at high capacity. 
Additionally, RL models face scalability issues, which lead to increased waiting times for resources in highly 
volatile environments. The main challenge for cloud service providers is efficiently allocating and utilizing cloud 
resources. These resources include VMs, CPUs, RAM, storage, bandwidth, and other components. Effective task 
scheduling techniques are required to manage these resources over the Internet in order to minimize energy 
consumption in cloud data centers. This in turn, helps reduce operational costs and environmental impact. 
On the other hand, from consumer’s perspective, energy-efficient task scheduling techniques must meet the 
consumer’s QoS requirements include response time, low makespan, and user satisfaction. The techniques 
must fulfill these demands stated in the SLA. Additionally, they should not impose any additional cost over the 
Internet and must be achieved in a dynamic fog-cloud environment. The aforementioned discussion motivates 
the authors to address these challenges, particularly the task scheduling problem, by proposing a suitable ML-
based task scheduling solution in a dynamic fog-cloud environment. Moving forward, we will address the 
following research question: “How can ML-based models be integrated to optimize resource scheduling and energy 
consumption in fog-cloud environments?”

Experimental setup
This section details the experimental setup for evaluating the proposed EcoTaskSched model in comparison 
to the baseline models in a fog-cloud computing environment. We conduct experiments using the COSCO 
framework, a physical testbed enabling single or multi-step simulations of container migration decisions in fog 
computing. To simulate real deployments, we setup a physical setup of 10 host VMs on the Microsoft Azure 
general purpose Bs-series to create heterogeneous fog-cloud testbed for large-scale experiments. Specifically, 
we use six lightweight VMs in the fog (edge) layer, hosted in the West UK datacenter, and four powerful VMs 
located in the US Central region, running on the Windows OS platform in the fog and cloud layer. Bs-series 
VMs offer a cost-effective option for workloads with low to moderate CPU usage, making them ideal for testing, 
development, low to medium-traffic web servers, and small to medium databases. We assume that all gateway 
connectivity devices are on the same LAN as the host server in the West UK region. Table 5 presents host 
configurations and pricing details (cost per hour in US Dollar) at the fog and cloud layer.
Similarly, the Defog benchmark is a suit of six real-time heterogeneous workloads used to generate 
workloads for training and evaluating the performance of the EcoTaskSched model against baseline models 
in fog computing. In a smart building, certain DeFog workloads are particularly relevant to heterogeneous IoT 
applications, such as video surveillance processing, environmental monitoring, and smart lighting control. 
We utilize three specific DeFog applications: the Yolo benchmark (compute-intensive, memory-intensive, and 
bandwidth-intensive), Aeneas benchmark (bandwidth-intensive), and PocketSphinx benchmark (compute-
intensive), which run workloads corresponding to a variety of heterogeneous IoT applications in a fog-cloud 
environment. Yolo and Aeneas runs with 1500 user requests, whereas PocketSphinx runs with 320 user requests. 
We use these different categories of workloads to generate training data and run our simulations. The dataset 
consists of workload information on resource utilization metrics for each time step, including the number of CPU 
cores requested, CPU frequency (MIPS), Disk read/write operations, RAM requested, and network bandwidth 
(receive/transmit) characteristics form VMs running on distributed datacenters. These recourse characteristics 
and workload data constitutes the features values set. Furthermore, the arrival of all independent tasks within 
a time period (scheduling interval (It)), follows a Poisson distribution, i.e., Poisson (λ) where λ = 1.2 jobs for 
|H|=10 and λ = 5 jobs for |H|=50. Here, H represents the number of virtualized host, with 10 hosts in the Azure 
physical setup and 50 hosts considered in a large-scale fog environment in the simulator. The task distribution 
and selection among the three DeFog applications (Yolo, Aeneas, and PocketSphinx) follow the probabilities 
(py, pa, ps) = 0.33 for each run. We conduct all experiments over 50 scheduling interval, where each interval lasts 
300 s. A total experiment time of 4 h and 10 min was consumed. To ensure statistical significance, we the results 
over five runs and use diverse workload scenarios (normal and intensive) to compare with the baseline models. 
We implemented the proposed algorithm and baseline models in Python (TensorFlow) using the COSCO 
framework and the DeFog benchmark, integrating CNN and BiLSTM models in a fog-cloud environment. All 
experiments were conducted on a computer system with the following hardware specifications: CPU (Intel i7-
10700 K), RAM (64GB), GPU (Nividia GTX 1060) and OS (Windows 10 Pro).

Results and discussion
In this section, we analyze and evaluate the results obtained from our proposed EcoTaskSched model using all 
the specified performance evaluation metrics. The primary objective of the EcoTaskSched model is to optimize 
task scheduling on the constrained resources of fog and cloud to reduce energy consumption, as expressed 
in Eq. (1) (the objective function), while ensuring QoS provisioning, as described in Eqs. (1a)-(1d), using a 
CNN-based model coupled with BiLSTM network. The experimental results of the EcoTaskSched model are 
quantified, visualized, and compared with baseline models, including the traditional GGCN25 and BiGGCN26. 
The detailed analysis is based on experiments conducted under various workload scenarios using the COSCO 
framework, a Python-based statistical library. The main advantage of using the COSCO library is its seamless 
integration of ML-based models for task scheduling in realistic fog-cloud environments. It supports simulations 
of complex scenarios and facilitates benchmarking and evaluation. Two types of scenarios were tested: a normal 
workload (with a mean of 2 tasks per interval) and an intensive workload (with a mean of 4 tasks per interval). 
Each scenario was tested on four standard Azure B2s virtualized host machines. Each experiment ran for 50 
scheduling intervals, with tasks generated and normally distributed using the DeFog benchmark.

Conclusion and future work
The integration of IoT technologies into fog-cloud computing networks provides practical solutions and 
adds multiple dimensions to the modern digital landscape. Cloud data centers deliver real-time data, and 
insights to service users, enabling monitoring, control, productivity improvements, and decision-making. 
This advancement also promotes environmental sustainability. However, this extensive traffic exchange raises 
concerns about the uniform allocation and efficient utilization of constrained resources (software, hardware, 
and third-party products) to ensure QoS parameters such as latency, energy consumption, job completion 
ratio, SLA, etc. in fog-cloud of IoT network. To address these challenges, we defined an objective function 
to reduce energy consumption while ensuring QoS provisioning in the fog-cloud of IoT network. Therefore, 
we proposed the EcoTaskSched model, which significantly enhances cloud stream processing by integrating 
advanced ML techniques, particularly CNN with BiLSTM network, to enable more efficient task scheduling. 
Meanwhile, the stable CNN model is employed to identify and extract feature sets from time-series workload 
tasks and constrained resources of the fog and cloud nodes. BiLSTM is integrated with the convolutional layers 
of the CNN model to capture both past and future dependencies in the input sequence. This enable efficient 
sequential decision-making in task scheduling and helps resolve the research problem. The research problem is 
mathematically expressed through an objective function, and a scheduling algorithm is developed to support the 
proposed methodology. This approach outperforms state-of-the-art models by reducing energy consumption, 
increasing job completion rates, minimizing SLA violations, lowering response rates, improving throughput, 
and reducing execution costs in a dynamic and heterogeneous fog-cloud IoT environment. Furthermore, the 
experimental results show that the EcoTaskSched model achieves an average energy consumption of 65.8 
kWh under normal workloads and 68.9 kWh under intensive conditions, significantly lower than that of the 
GGCN and BiGGCN models. Additionally, the EcoTaskSched model consistently achieved a high average job 
completion rate of 85% under normal workloads and 84.5% intensive workload conditions, surpassing GGCN 
(64% and 69%) and BiGGCN (73% and 77%). Similarly, the EcoTaskSched model has lower SLA violation 
rates and average response times compared to the other baseline models. The EcoTaskSched model reduces 
execution costs by 36% and 35%, outperforming the baseline models. Furthermore, it achieves the highest 
average throughput across all configurations of virtualized hosts compared to the other two models. Based on 
these significant improvements in the required parameters achieved by the proposed model, we conclude that 
the objective function effectively addresses the research problem in the fog-cloud IoT network.
In future research, we will focus on further validating the EcoTaskSched model through real-world IoT 
applications in cloud and fog environments of varying scales. Also, investigating the model’s scalability and 
robustness across diverse conditions and operations will be essential. Additionally, integrating AI models with 
other advanced ML techniques could further enhance business process design.
